clue.text: Murder investigation's beginning with detectives in house

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word for house

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: beginning asks for just the opening letter of investigation

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: A murder inquiry gets under way with police officers arriving at a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I (the start of 'investigation's') plus CID inside HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is the legal term for the killing of one person by another.

clue.text: Fit of anger gets little man taken off the board

parts.note: a huff is a sulky fit of pique
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A small man loses his temper on being removed from the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: In draughts (checkers), a piece is huffed when it is removed for failing to capture.
explanation.definitionFit: In draughts a huffed piece is one forfeited and removed as a penalty.

clue.text: Venom gets rodents — almost all being caught

indicators.note: being caught means the shortened word is trapped inside the rodents

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of all

explanation.surface: Poison is laid down and nearly every rat is trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL, and 'being caught' puts it inside MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in the figurative sense is spite or ill will.

clue.text: Nasty job imposed on me? It's a breeze!

definitions.meaning: a dupe made to do someone else's dirty work, like the cat in the fable pulling chestnuts from the fire
a light puff of wind that ruffles calm water

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a horrible task, then boasts it was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a breeze' looks like 'it's easy' but means a literal light wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used as a tool by another is one sense; a slight ripple-making wind is the sailing sense.

clue.text: More laddies sadly becoming brassed off

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of More laddies end up in a sorry new order

explanation.surface: More young men are feeling fed up and gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MORE LADDIES; 'brassed off' is British slang for fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoralised means disheartened, having lost confidence and spirit.

clue.text: Fodder I left for wise man to eat

indicators.note: to eat means the word for wise man takes the other letters into its mouth

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Someone leaves fodder out for a wise old man's supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts I and L (left) inside SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented grass or crops stored as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Repeat line forgotten by educated person

indicators.note: forgotten by means the line letter is dropped from the word for educated person

parts.note: a literate is one who can read and write, an educated person

explanation.surface: A learned man keeps having to go over a line he forgot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten by' removes L from LITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again.

clue.text: Like some betting with a lot spent foolishly — pounds wasted

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters of a lot spent are jumbled
wasted says the pounds letter is thrown away from the jumble

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A gambler squanders a large sum, losing money on a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges A LOT SPENT, and 'wasted' removes the L (pounds) from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-post bets are placed in advance of race day, before the runners are finalised.

clue.text: New deal secures gold — then there's party in affluent place

indicators.note: secures means the jumbled letters hold the word for gold inside them
New signals the letters of deal take a fresh order

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A fresh contract brings in gold, then celebrations in a rich town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DEAL to ELDA, and 'secures' places OR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by explorers, now any place of great wealth.

clue.text: Occupied for the whole week — after which the field can be left?

definitions.meaning: employed for a complete working week, as opposed to part-time

definitions.text: after which the field can be left?
definitions.meaning: the final whistle at the end of a football match, when players leave the pitch

explanation.surface: A worker kept busy all week looks forward to leaving the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is sporting: in football the referee blows for the end of the game, and the teams then walk off.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a job filling the standard working week; the other is the end of a match's playing time.

clue.text: Having a waistcoat already acquired

definitions.meaning: a vest is the American word for a waistcoat, so wearing one
legally secured, as with rights or interests already held

explanation.surface: A man in a waistcoat already owns what he wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English a vest is a waistcoat; vested interests are ones already settled on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a vest (US waistcoat) is one sense; rights fixed and held without condition is the legal sense.

clue.text: One gets away to frolic alongside English society

parts.note: to caper is to skip about playfully

explanation.surface: Someone slips off to have fun among fashionable English society.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaper is a person who breaks free or flees.

clue.text: Musical performer following wife in loose gown

indicators.note: following says the performer comes after the letter for wife

parts.note: a rapper is a hip-hop performer

explanation.surface: A singer comes in behind his wife, who is dressed in a loose gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a light dressing gown or robe worn wrapped around the body.

clue.text: Band at the match

parts.note: match read as a marriage, and band as a ring of metal rather than musicians at a game

explanation.surface: Musicians play at the football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians and 'match' a sporting fixture, but a match is also a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding ring is the band given at a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: What you may see in Derbyshire village from may is smart

definitions.text: What you may see in Derbyshire village from may
definitions.meaning: Derbyshire villages decorate their wells with pictures made of flowers such as may blossom
elegantly turned out in good clothes

explanation.surface: A visitor to Derbyshire admires something smart made of hawthorn blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' is hawthorn blossom, not the month; Derbyshire is an English county famous for the custom of decorating wells with flower pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated well is the Derbyshire custom; a smartly clothed person is the everyday sense.

clue.text: Vessel child would go in by preference

indicators.note: would go in places the child's letters inside the other word

parts.note: sooner, as in would sooner, means rather

explanation.surface: A youngster would rather get into the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would go in' puts CH inside SOONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship; also a tall glass.

clue.text: Arrested supporters got up and ran away

indicators.note: in a down clue got up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: fans are supporters
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: Arrested fans rose up and escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns FANS around to SNAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaffled is informal for seized or nabbed.

clue.text: Support provided after power strike?

parts.note: when a strike cuts the electricity, people light wax sources and need a holder for them; also a strike of a match

explanation.surface: Workers walk out at the power station and help is laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' is a holder, not aid; 'power strike' is industrial action cutting the electricity, after which you'd light a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A candlestick is the holder that supports a candle, used when the lights go out.

clue.text: The French composer gets little right — one needing teacher?

parts.note: le is French for the
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: A French composer achieves little and needs teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: Arne, the eighteenth-century composer of Rule, Britannia!, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil or student needs someone to instruct them.

clue.text: Continues confining boy under part of castle

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the boy below the castle part

parts.note: the keep is a castle's central tower
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is kept locked in the dungeon below the castle tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confining' sets the scene of a boy shut in the keep; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeps on means carries on or persists.

clue.text: Ladies on the catwalk seldom slovenly

indicators.note: slovenly signals the letters of seldom are untidily rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashion models are rarely scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slovenly' rearranges SELDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who parade clothes on a fashion runway are mannequins.

clue.text: Some great students selected for good breeding?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some top scholars are picked because of their fine pedigree.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion kept for breeding is said to stand in that role.

clue.text: Most distant worker is free and easy

parts.note: off means the far side, as in the off side of a road or horse
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: The farthest-away employee is relaxed about everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most distant' gives OFF in its sense of farther away, as in the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand describes a casual, unconcerned manner.

clue.text: Leaves the house and loses any glow

definitions.meaning: a fire or light that dies is extinguished

explanation.surface: Someone leaves home and their radiance fades.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping outdoors is one sense; a flame or lamp becoming extinguished is the other.

clue.text: Stockings fitting Lynn so badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of Lynn so are put in a poor order

explanation.surface: Some hosiery is a poor fit for a woman called Lynn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges LYNN SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made from the synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Young girl confined — so that her youth can't be this?

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
pent, as in pent up, means shut in

explanation.surface: A girl kept locked away cannot waste her young years.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'misspent youth': a girl shut away has no chance to squander her early years.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspent youth is one wasted on idle pursuits, which confinement would prevent.

clue.text: Hunters? They could be dressed in red, sir!

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters of red and sir are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Fox hunters traditionally wear red coats, addressed respectfully as sir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be dressed' rearranges RED and SIR; huntsmen famously wear red (hunting pink) coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox hunters go on horseback, so a hunter is one kind of rider, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Diagnose disease which make you very worried?

indicators.note: disease read as dis-ease, putting the letters of Diagnose out of their comfortable order

explanation.surface: A doctor's diagnosis of illness leaves the patient anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disease' rearranges DIAGNOSE; 'which make you' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means suffering great anguish or distress.
